# Earthquake in Chile - On Monday 1st March, the copper price hit a 5-week peak of $7,600/t in early trading at the LME due to supply worries following the 8.8 magnitude earthquake that hit Chile on Saturday 27th February 2010. Most major copper operations are located in the northern regions. - Northern regions: CRU understands that roads and ports are in good condition. All indications are that there has been no substantial loss of production. Interruption to shipments for contractual obligations is a possibility. There has been minor damage to power generation facilities but potential problems with transmission and distribution of electricity may affect some operations. Also, shortage of diesel is a possibility, which would halt power generation at mines that rely on diesel generators. Key copper ports of Antofagasta and Mejillones are said to be operating normally. - Southern regions: Questions remain over the condition of the country’s roads, ports, railways, bridges and harbours. Reports are limited and mixed regarding these logistical facilities. Copper operations have not suffered major damage, but those located near Santiago (El Teniente, Andina, El Soldado, Los Bronces mines; and Chagres smelters) halted production due the power cut on Saturday. It was reported, however, that on Sunday afternoon they started to resume operations. The copper port of San Antonio is closed. Roads that connect Santiago with the south of the country have been affected. The road from Santiago to Rancagua was damaged; access has been resumed but is slow at certain points. Access to El Teniente is via this highway. - The big question is about the state of the country’s power facilities. Problems at the nation’s oil refineries could conceivably disrupt supplies to generators. It was reported that state oil company ENAP suspended operations at its Bнo Bнo (damage to infrastructure) and Aconcagua (power shortages) refineries, which are located south from Santiago and are the only refineries in Chile. ENAP assured consumers that it has a ten-day supply of fuels and is increasing imports and the company has already started to import diesel to meet demand. © 2010 CRU International Limited **confidential** Copper Monitor www.crumonitor.com After the 10-day stock runs out, there is a possibility that the company will be challenged to keep supplying the country. - BHP Billiton, Barrick Gold, Xstrata and Teck all stated that their operations have not suffered any damage as off Monday 1st mid-day London time.
